aboutH2: Red Road North: Residential Addiction Treatment in Terrace, BC
intro: Red Road North is a 12-bed residential addiction treatment centre outside Terrace, in Northwest British Columbia. Red Road Recovery runs it in partnership with the Northern First Nations Alliance (NFNA), and it opened with a ceremony on December 2, 2025. Residents live in a wood-sided house on a riverfront acreage off Highway 16 East, where a forest trail leads down to the Skeena River.

The program is the same one Red Road Recovery runs in the Shuswap and the Okanagan: counselling one-on-one and in groups, recovery education and an introduction to the 12 Steps, alongside Indigenous cultural practice led by local partners. It is co-ed, for adults 19 and over, and staffed 24/7. Stays run 30, 45, 60 or 90 days, and some beds are publicly funded for BC residents.

pillars.title: A Riverfront Acreage on the Skeena
pillars.body: Red Road North sits on acreage along Highway 16 East outside Terrace, behind a carved wooden gate with a wolf and a bear cut into it. Red Road Recovery calls the property a riverfront acreage, and a trail through cedar and spruce leads down to the Skeena River. Inside, the house is finished in wood, with a large lounge hung with Northwest Coast formline art, a separate group room, a small counselling office and shared bedrooms. Terrace itself is the main service town for the Skeena region, with Kitimat to the south and the Nass Valley to the north.

pillars.title: Counselling, the 12 Steps and Cultural Practice
pillars.body: Red Road Recovery describes its program as whole-person and biopsychosocial. Residents work with counsellors one-on-one and in groups, take part in recovery education and practical skill building, and get an introduction to the 12 Steps. Cultural programming depends on the location and on what community partners guide, and the list Red Road Recovery publishes includes smudging, medicine wheel teachings, land-based activities, spiritual guidance from Elders and Knowledge Keepers, and sweat lodge ceremonies. At Red Road North that work is done with the Northern First Nations Alliance.

pillars.title: A Small Team With Lived Experience
pillars.body: Red Road Recovery says every member of its staff has personal experience of recovery, on top of their training. At Red Road North, Interim Executive Director Deana Slack is a certified drug and alcohol counsellor and medication-assisted treatment specialist with Coast Salish roots. Counsellor Cheryl Gray holds a Master of Social Work and has trained in CBT, DBT and Motivational Interviewing, with a focus on trauma, grief and brain injury. The full Red Road North team page is on the centre's website.

overviewH2: Red Road North: Who It Is For and How It Is Funded
overview: Red Road North was planned with the Northwest in mind. Coverage of the opening by the Nisga'a Lisims Government said it serves Northwest First Nations community members and other people in the area, and CFTK News reported that it takes local residents as well as people from across the province. The Province's March 2026 announcement placed its 12 land-based treatment beds inside the Indigenous Treatment and Recovery Program. Red Road Recovery does not publish any rule limiting who may attend beyond age and, for funded beds, BC residency.

location.heading: Red Road North in Terrace, British Columbia
location.intro: Red Road North is on Highway 16 East outside Terrace, in the Skeena region of Northern BC. From Vancouver it is about 15 hours by road, so most people fly from YVR to Northwest Regional Airport (Terrace-Kitimat) in under two hours; Kitimat is about 45 minutes away, Prince Rupert about 1.5 hours west and Prince George roughly 7 hours east.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What kind of program is Red Road North?
faqs.a: Red Road North is a 12-bed residential addiction treatment centre for adults, run by Red Road Recovery in partnership with the Northern First Nations Alliance (NFNA). Residents live on site, and Red Road Recovery says its residences are staffed 24/7. The home is registered with the BC assisted living registry as a supportive recovery residence, and the treatment program holds CARF accreditation.

Red Road North is at 20047 Highway 16 East, on a riverfront acreage outside Terrace in Northwest BC. Local news coverage places it on the Skeena River. Terrace is about 15 hours by road from Vancouver, so most people from the Lower Mainland fly into Northwest Regional Airport (Terrace-Kitimat).

Red Road Recovery offers residential programs of 30, 45, 60 and 90 days. Coverage of the Terrace opening described Red Road North's program as 90 days, so ask the admissions team which lengths are open at this location when you apply.

faqs.q: How much does Red Road North cost?
faqs.a: Red Road Recovery does not publish prices; it asks you to contact the team for private pricing. It also lists publicly funded beds at no cost for BC residents over 19, funded through a CMHA grant, with 23 such beds across its network. Private stays can be paid by the person, family, a First Nations band, insurance or an employer.

faqs.q: Can First Nations clients get funding?
faqs.a: Yes. Red Road Recovery says subsidy for its program is available through the First Nations Health Authority (FNHA), and First Nation bands can buy contracted beds at a discounted rate to avoid waitlists. The Province also announced in March 2026 that Red Road North's 12 land-based treatment beds are part of its Indigenous Treatment and Recovery Program.

The residential program is co-ed and for adults 19 and over. Publicly funded beds require BC residency, while privately funded beds are open to anyone. The Nisga'a Lisims Government's coverage of the opening said the centre was built with Northwest First Nations communities in mind, and Red Road Recovery does not publish any other eligibility limits.

faqs.q: Does Red Road North offer detox?
faqs.a: Red Road Recovery's own website does not describe a detox or withdrawal management service at Red Road North, and recovery.com lists detox as not offered. A December 2025 article from the Nisga'a Lisims Government mentioned withdrawal management, so call 250-800-3190 to ask what medical support is in place before you arrive.

The program combines individual and group counselling, recovery education, practical skill building and an introduction to the 12 Steps with Indigenous cultural supports. Depending on the location and the guidance of community partners, Red Road Recovery lists smudging, medicine wheel teachings, land-based activities, time with Elders and Knowledge Keepers, and sweat lodge ceremonies. In-house chefs cook the meals.

Yes. CARF lists Red Road North under its residential treatment program for adults with substance use disorders, with a Three-Year Accreditation. Red Road Recovery says the three-year award covers all of its locations.

Apply through the Apply Now page on redroadrecovery.com, call 250-800-3190 or email contact@redroadrecovery.com. Red Road Recovery asks that completed applications go to its central fax at 1-250-410-3448. FNHA subsidy applications are linked from the Funding Options page.
